title: Beliefs and Behavior in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.07943v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: There is significant uncertainty about whether abstractions like beliefs or desires usefully describe the behavior of large language models (LLMs). In addition to the inherent scientific interest of this question, these latent quantities are often invoked to explain the behavior of LLMs to users or to define and evaluate harmful behaviors which are relative to intent. Nevertheless, we currently lack a means to systematically test whether concepts like "belief" are well-applied to LLMs, and hence whether they are likely to be fruitful ingredients of attempts to align models with human interests. We propose an approach for empirically studying such questions, asking whether a single latent variable inferred from the LLMs' outputs -- interpreted as a degree of belief -- allows an observer to make interpretable predictions of how the LLMs' will respond to new prompts. translated_title: 语言模型中的信念与行为
translated_abstract: 关于信念或欲望等抽象概念是否能有效描述大语言模型（LLM）的行为，目前存在很大的不确定性。除了这个问题本身的科学意义之外，这些潜在变量常被用来向用户解释LLM的行为，或用于定义和评估与意图相关的有害行为。然而，我们目前缺乏一种系统性方法来检验“信念”等概念是否适用于LLM，以及它们是否可能成为使模型与人类利益对齐工作中有价值的要素。我们提出了一种实证研究此类问题的方法，探讨从LLM输出中推断出的单一潜在变量——被解释为信念程度——是否能让观察者对LLM将如何响应新提示做出可解释的预测。我们发现，高性能模型可以被有效地描述为持有信念……
tldr: 本文提出一种实证方法，检验“信念”这一潜在变量能否用于描述大语言模型的行为，发现高性能模型可以被有效地描述为持有信念，这为理解和对齐LLM行为提供了新途径。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an empirical approach testing whether a latent variable interpreted as "degree of belief" can usefully describe LLM behavior, finding that highly capable models are usefully described as holding beliefs, which offers a new pathway for understanding and aligning LLMs.
